summary: `inventory-worker` is installed on node1 as an enabled, long-running systemd service. It runs under a dedicated unprivileged account, has no capabilities or privilege escalation, and its filesystem namespace permits writes only within `/var/lib/inventory`. The service and its data recovered after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created the `inventory-worker` system account and `/var/lib/inventory` state directory.
Installed the background worker and enabled its systemd service.
Applied `NoNewPrivileges`, an empty capability bounding set, a read-only root filesystem, and a writable exception for `/var/lib/inventory`.
Verified live writes succeed inside the permitted directory and fail outside it.
Safely restarted node1, confirmed its boot identity changed, and verified service and data recovery.

evidence.summary: The service is enabled and active; its heartbeat log advanced while running and gained a new start record after reboot.
Before and after reboot, namespace probes wrote successfully inside the inventory directory while writes to /tmp and another /var/lib path were blocked.
systemd reports NoNewPrivileges=yes and CapabilityBoundingSet=0; the live process has zero permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capabilities.

Healthy baseline boot ID a9593011-3617-4b72-8b02-2e8a4d2b17a3 was captured; safe reboot acknowledgement returned; the new boot ID is 9d420b05-b6bc-4c2f-90d6-351c611991a5; system state, service, historical log data, and persisted probe recovered.
